items.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026
items.q: The interviewee discusses Milt Hinton only in response to the interviewer's generalization about 'classy guys' like Joe Wilder and Milt Hinton. The interviewee does not mention any personal interaction, meeting, or specific relationship with Milt Hinton, responding instead with a general philosophic

ctx.x: that Joe Williams was playing at a club there. So I said, “Hey Mom, we’re going out tonight.” And then she said, “Well where are we going?” I said, “You don’t worry about it,” you know, “just come on.” And then as we are getting ready she said, “Oh where is he playing?” She knew that that must have been why I was taking her out. So I said, “Yeah, okay you got it.” So I tipped the maître d – I guess he wouldn’t have been maître d – the waiter or the guy who met us there because – was it a restaurant? Yeah, maybe.…

Indeed. He was a classy guy. And he also was a good example, I’ve noticed with, I mentioned Joe Wilder, and Milt Hinton, they all had this thing that they were wonderful people, friendly. But at the same time they had so much pride in what they did, like don’t mess with that. Don’t disrespect what they do or you’ll be sorry. I mean they would react to something where they were being taken advantage of. They weren’t the kind of people that were just so nice that you could do anything and take advantage of them.…

Well we musn’t think that because somebody is nice that they can’t take care of themselves. In fact I think for my life I keep myself in very excellent physical condition and study martial arts since I was a teenager, and the point is to lead a gentle life, to be a nice person, to not have to be mean to people or to be like this or any of that kind of stuff. Be nice and loving. To not have to descend to somebody else’s level if they want to insult me or something like that. You know to be above all of these things.
